findings.title: Targets are now interpolated two to three times before being sent
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now maps every target through `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`, but the same method is still applied later by `DataSourceWithBackend.query()` for every target of the sub-request created in `runSplitGroupedQueries` (via `datasource.runQuery`). In the shard-splitting path it is worse: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates once (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52) and then calls `runSplitQuery` for each shard group, which interpolates again, and the backend wrapper interpolates a third time. Concrete consequences: (1) `applyTemplateVariables` calls `addAdHocFilters`, so ad hoc filters are re-applied to an expression that already contains them; for non-indexed labels the filter is appended as a pipeline stage, producing duplicated stages such as `| env="prod" | env="prod"` in the executed query; (2) `templateSrv.replace` runs over already-substituted text, so any variable value that itself contains `$name`/`${name}` syntax is substituted a second time and the resulting query differs from what the user wrote; (3) each pass re-parses the LogQL expression (lezer) per sub-request, which is pure overhead – the updated shard test even asserts 5 calls where there was previously 1. Consider adding an option/flag so the splitting code interpolates exactly once (e.g. skip interpolation in nested `runSplitQuery` calls and in the request sent to the backend).

findings.title: New interpolation test asserts behaviour that does not hold with the real template service
findings.body: The test stubs `replace` with a blind `input.replace('$__auto', '5m')`, and then asserts that the expression sent to `runQuery` is `count_over_time({a="b"}[5m])`. The real Loki `applyTemplateVariables` deliberately strips `__auto`/`__interval`/`__range` from the scoped vars handed to `templateSrv.replace` so that those variables are interpolated on the backend with the *split* time range; with the production template service `$__auto` would still be present in the expression at this point. The test therefore encodes incorrect expectations and gives false confidence. It also does not cover the regression the PR fixes: that the interpolated `step` is used when computing the partitions (e.g. asserting the number/size of sub-requests changes when `step: '$step'` resolves to a large interval). The same applies to the equivalent new test in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts.
